subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that the points A(2i−j+k), B(i−3j−5k) and C(3i−4j−4k) are the vertices of a right-angled triangle.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show these three points make a right-angled triangle.

steps.label: Find the side vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Go round the triangle: AB, then BC, then CA. Going round means each vector ends where the next begins, so none of the three sides is missed.

recall.must_convey: That the three side vectors AB, BC and CA are found by subtracting position vectors, going round the triangle.
accept: find AB BC and CA by subtracting the position vectors going round the triangle
each side is the far point minus the near point, taken in order
work out the three sides AB BC CA
AB BC CA ni position vectors subtract chesi kanukovali
go round the triangle taking differences

steps.why: Taking the sides in a cycle guarantees you have all three and no repeats. Picking AB, AC and BC would give the same triangle but makes the next comparison harder to read.
common_mistakes: Subtracting the wrong way round on one side.
Computing AB, AC and BC and then comparing the wrong pair.

steps.label: Find the magnitudes
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Square each component, add, take the root. Leave the answers as surds — squaring them again in the next step is easier from √41 than from 6.4.

recall.must_convey: That each side length is the square root of the sum of the squares of its components, giving √41, √6 and √35.
accept: take the square root of the sum of the squares of the components for each side, giving root forty one root six and root thirty five
find the magnitude of each vector as a surd
the three lengths are root forty one, root six and root thirty five
prathi vector magnitude root gaa rasi, root 41, root 6, root 35 vasthai
square the components, add, and take the root

steps.why: Leaving the lengths as surds is deliberate: the test compares SQUARES, and the square of √41 is just 41.
common_mistakes: Losing a sign before squaring — every square is positive.
Turning the surds into decimals and then failing to match exactly.

steps.label: Check Pythagoras
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Square the three lengths and look for the one that equals the sum of the other two. Here 41 = 6 + 35, so AB is the hypotenuse.

recall.must_convey: That the squares are compared and the longest side squared equals the sum of the other two squares — 41 = 6 + 35.
accept: square them and forty one equals six plus thirty five so Pythagoras holds
the square of the longest side equals the sum of the other two squares
AB squared is forty one which is six plus thirty five
forty one equals six plus thirty five, so Pythagoras satisfy avthundi
check the Pythagoras relation on the squares

steps.why: The converse of Pythagoras is what is being used: if the squares fit, the triangle IS right-angled. You are not assuming a right angle and checking — you are proving one exists.
common_mistakes: Testing the wrong side as the hypotenuse; it must be the longest.
Comparing the lengths rather than their squares.

steps.label: Conclude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Name the conclusion, and it is worth naming WHERE the right angle is: opposite the longest side, so at C.
lines: The relation holds, so the angle opposite AB is 90°.

lines.text: ∴ A, B, C are the vertices of a right-angled triangle.

recall.must_convey: That because the Pythagoras relation holds, the three points form a right-angled triangle.
accept: since the relation holds the three points form a right angled triangle
Pythagoras is satisfied so it is a right angled triangle
the points A B C make a right angled triangle
relation satisfy ayindi kabatti right angled triangle
therefore the triangle is right angled

steps.why: The right angle sits at the vertex the hypotenuse does not touch. Saying so shows the relation was understood rather than pattern-matched.
common_mistakes: Writing "hence proved" without naming the triangle.
Claiming the right angle is at A or B.
